question_title: How to get past Confirm Security Exception
question_content: Thunderbird has worked fine for me over the years. I rarely send mail but started receiving a message that smpt server refused connection and contacted Network Solutions support. Their advice is below but I have clicked Clear Security Exception many times but can't get beyond it. Any ideas would be welcome. To configure your mailbox in Thunderbird, please follow these steps:    Open the Thunderbird application.    Select Add Mail Account.    Enter your Full Name, Email Address, and Password.    Click Continue.     When you reach the page titled "Connect your email settings", click Edit Configuration.    Change both the Incoming Server Hostname and Outgoing Server Hostname to mymail2.myregisteredsite.com.    Click Connect.    Enter your mailbox password when prompted.    After entering the password, a warning message may appear. Select Confirm Security Exception.  Please note that you may need to click Confirm Security Exception three or four times before the account setup is completed successfully. The reason you are receiving the security warning is that the mailbox is configured to use Connection Security: None. This is necessary because your mailbox is hosted on a legacy email service that is not compatible with SSL/TLS or STARTTLS encrypted connection methods. As a result, Thunderbird may display security warnings during the configuration process. If you require further assistance with Thunderbird configuration, we recommend contacting your personal IT professional or someone familiar with email client setup and administration, as third-party email client configuration falls outside our support scope.

question_title: Thunderbird 153 ESR freezes during POP3 mail retrieval and while idle on Windows 10
question_content: Hello, I am experiencing repeated freezes in Thunderbird 153 ESR on Windows 10. I have been investigating this problem since mid-October 2026, but have not been able to identify the cause. Thunderbird is essential for my daily work, so I would appreciate advice on identifying the cause and restoring stable operation. 1. System environment - PC: dynabook R63/B - OS: Windows 10, 64-bit - Thunderbird: 153.6.0esr, 64-bit - Mail provider: @nifty (Japan) - Incoming mail: POP3 over SSL/TLS, port 995 - Security software: Super Security (Japanese security software) - Mail storage: Local mbox files 2. When the problem started Thunderbird worked reasonably well until September 2026. The freezing problem began around mid-October 2026. Windows Reliability Monitor recorded Thunderbird as "Stopped responding" on October 19, 2026, at 9:48 a.m. This is the earliest recorded incident I have found, although the problem may have started earlier. Thunderbird update history: - September 18: 153.3.1esr - October 1: 153.4.0esr - October 14: 153.5.0esr - October 21: 153.5.1esr - October 28: 153.6.0esr The first recorded freeze occurred after the update to 153.5.0esr. However, I have not established that the update caused the problem. 3. Symptoms Thunderbird becomes unresponsive and usually has to be forcibly terminated. During these freezes, Windows Task Manager often shows Thunderbird using approximately 30–40% CPU, repeatedly around 39–40%. Freezes also occur when Thunderbird is using only about 1.1 GB of memory. On other occasions, memory usage has increased to approximately 2.56 GB. The problem occurs under several different conditions: 1. During manual POP3 mail retrieval. 2. After repeated manual mail retrieval operations. 3. Approximately 30 minutes after a single mail retrieval, even when Thunderbird is left idle. 4. Sometimes after replying to messages or copying messages to other folders. 5. In both normal mode and Troubleshoot Mode. 6. Sometimes during the first mail retrieval after starting Thunderbird. Other Windows applications generally remain responsive when Thunderbird freezes. Restarting Windows sometimes restores normal Thunderbird operation temporarily, but the problem returns. 4. Troubleshooting already performed I have already tried the following: - Reinstalled Thunderbird from the official website. - Created a new Thunderbird test profile. - Disabled extensions. - Disabled hardware acceleration. - Disabled global search and indexing. - Removed all active Thunderbird message filters for testing. - Disabled the anti-spam component of Super Security. - Disabled automatic mail checking and automatic downloading. - Tested manual mail retrieval in Troubleshoot Mode. - Reduced the size of the Inbox from approximately 4.1 GB to 2.4 GB. - Performed a full antivirus scan, which detected no threats. The new profile initially worked, including several successful POP3 retrievals, but the freezing problem later returned. Reinstalling Thunderbird did not resolve the issue. The anti-spam component remains disabled for testing, but the problem continues. 5. Windows error records Windows Reliability Monitor recorded Thunderbird as unresponsive on October 19, 2026, at 9:48 a.m. Windows Event Viewer also recorded an Application Hang, Event ID 1002, on October 30, 2026, at approximately 4:23 a.m. The affected executable was thunderbird.exe, version 153.6.0.0. These records confirm the application hang but do not identify its underlying cause. 6. POP3 communication Earlier POP3 logging confirmed that Thunderbird connected to the @nifty POP3 server and received a CAPA response. However, I have not identified which POP3 or internal Thunderbird operation was active at the exact moment of the freeze. I have not collected a process memory dump. 7. Potentially related Mozilla bug reports I found two reports that may be relevant: - Bug 2080699: POP mail retrieval becomes unresponsive in Thunderbird 153.4.0esr. - Bug 2031744: Freezing potentially related to mail index (.msf) files and background processing. Some symptoms are similar, but I cannot determine whether they have the same underlying cause. 8. Questions I would appreciate advice on the following: 1. Are there known POP3-related freezes or high-CPU problems in Thunderbird 153 ESR, particularly after the October 2026 updates? 2. Could background mail processing, folder maintenance, or mail index files explain a freeze that occurs while Thunderbird is idle? 3. Could interaction with antivirus software or Windows networking components cause these symptoms? 4. Are there diagnostic steps that can help identify the cause without repeatedly freezing Thunderbird or risking existing mail data? 5. Would this information be more appropriate as an additional comment on an existing Bugzilla report or as a separate bug report? I have already spent considerable time testing different configurations. I would prefer to avoid repeating tests that have not helped. I have a backup of my Thunderbird profile and would like to preserve my existing mail data. Thank you for your assistance.
